svg.text: Design equations and the ten test speeds
Hydrokinetic Power – Working Equations and Test Matrix
INDICATIVE ARTIST'S ILLUSTRATION – NOT TO SCALE
Dimensions to be confirmed by survey and detailed design
P = ½ · ρ · A · U³ · Cp
P power at the rotor, W ρ fluid density, kg/m³ A swept area, m² U flow speed, m/s Cp power coefficient
Betz limit: Cp,max = 16 ⁄ 27 = 0.593 AFE design value: Cp = 0.35 (shrouded 0.35–0.45, Darrieus 0.20–0.35)
ρ sea ⁄ ρ air = 1 025 ⁄ 1.225 ≈ 837 ⇒ equal power per m² at U water = U wind ÷ ∛837 ≈ U wind ÷ 9.4
A 12 m/s wind and a 1.3 m/s current carry about the same power per square metre.
ROTOR SIZE FOR A TARGET OUTPUT
A = P ⁄ (½ · ρ · U³ · Cp) D = 2 · √(A ⁄ π) e.g. 100 kW at 2.5 m/s: A = 35.7 m², D = 6.7 m
λ = ω · R ⁄ U n = 60 · λ · U ⁄ (2 · π · R) λ 1.5–2.5 for slow spirals, 4–6 for tri-blade rotors → 30–60 rpm at the hub
U ≈ drift distance ⁄ time: 100 m in 60 s = 1.67 m/s ≈ 3.2 kn 1 kn = 0.514 m/s
TEN TEST SPEEDS – POWER PER m² OF ROTOR (ρ 1 025, Cp 0.35)
– Power rises with the cube of speed: doubling the current gives eight times the power per square metre.
– The ten test speeds are the laboratory and field matrix for the prototype programme with AetherFab at the University of Melbourne.
– Wind comparison uses the same Cp for both machines and is illustrative only.
